candidates.title: Exploring Model Invariance with Discrete Search for Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
candidates.abstract: As language models continue to grow in size due to their success in a wide range of applications such as conversational agents and coding, there is a pressing need to make them more accessible. A popular technique is to reduce their memory footprint by post-training quantization, where we use fewer bits (e.g., 4--8 bits) to represent the model without retraining it. However, quantizing language models remains a challenging task, especially in the ultra-low-bit setup (e.g., 2 bits). In this paper, we propose InvarExplore, a unified framework that systematically explores different kinds of model invariance to maximize quantization performance. Importantly, InvarExplore features a discrete search algorithm that enables us to explore permutation invariance, which is under-studied as it cannot be optimized with gradient-based methods. Such exploration allows us to take advantage of the synergy between each type of invariance. Our results and in-depth analyses show that InvarExplore is compatible with existing state-of-the-art integer quantization methods, achieving an add-on performance improvement over strong competing methods.
candidates.reason: InvarExploreは置換不変性等のモデル不変性を離散探索で同時活用する2bit級の超低ビットpost-training quantizationをLLM向けに提案し、既存PTQへの上乗せ改善を示す推論向け量子化の直接的貢献である。
